Readiness: verify each dependency; ``503`` if any is down (Doc 04 §22).

The §29 partial-success envelope.

Bulk progress lives here rather than on ``GET /jobs/{uuid}`` (Doc 04 §30): that surface is
gated by ``system:read`` (§22) and ``job_metadata`` carries no organization, so it can serve
neither a ``contacts:write`` operator nor tenant scoping. This mirrors the import/export
poll endpoints §14.1 already defines.

get.description: Stored health — cheap and always available. Use ``/refresh`` to re-pull from Meta.

Echo ``hub.challenge`` when ``hub.verify_token`` matches (Doc 04 §23).

Meta requires the bare challenge as the body — not JSON, not an envelope — or it refuses to
activate the subscription.

post.summary: Receive inbound messages & status callbacks (public, signature-gated)
post.description: Persist the delivery and ack; processing happens on the ``webhooks.*`` queues.

React to a message, or clear a reaction with an empty emoji (Doc 04 §18.2 v1.4).

A reaction is free-form (needs the open 24-hour window); it is accepted then delivered through
SendService → the Meta adapter exactly like a send — ``202`` with ``wamid`` null.

get.description: What the channel told us about this message, in the order it told us (Doc 03 §9.3).

post.description: Enqueue the sync and return immediately — no Meta call on this path.

get.description:
Pure render (FR-TPL-08): nothing is stored and nothing is sent.

Sample values ride the query string (`?body=Priya&body=%231234`) because Doc 04 §15 makes this
a `GET` — it is a projection of the template, not a change to it.

post.description: Creates the draft **and** materializes its roster, so the response counts are real.
Reads the materialized roster: the preview shows what will be sent, not a fresh query.

post.summary: Pre-send cost estimate from the rate card
post.description:
Price the materialized roster from the rate card (FR-CAM-11; Doc 04 §17).

No body: the estimate is derived from what would actually be sent, not a fresh audience query.
An empty or incomplete card answers `422 rate_card_not_configured` rather than a misleading
partial total. The endpoint stays on `campaigns:read` because its only write is caching the
quote on the campaign's own row (Doc 03 §8.5.5).

Validate and enqueue. The template and number are re-checked here, not just at create:
Meta may have paused the template since the draft was written.

Write the schedule and park the campaign in ``scheduled``. Nothing fires on this path:
``scheduler.tick`` reads the row when it comes due (Doc 06 §10.2 — the DB is the schedule).
Flips the switch every send reads. In-flight tasks are not chased — they will decline.
Re-dispatches; planning only ever picks up what still owes a send, so nothing repeats.

post.summary: Cancel a campaign and stop pending sends

post.description: Resets failed recipients and re-dispatches; the retry engine judges each attempt afresh.

get.description:
The inbox, newest activity first (Doc 04 §18.1).

Cursor-paginated by ``last_message_at``; filtered by status/assignee/number and searched by
``q`` (the customer's name or number) — exactly the frozen filter set, nothing more.
A thread's messages, newest first, cursor-paginated over the partitioned ledger.

post.description: Hand a thread to a user. The target must be an active member of the org (else 422).
Move the thread to open/pending/resolved/snoozed. Snoozed carries no timer this milestone.

Reset the thread's shared unread counter to zero (Doc 04 §18.1).

Read state is the denormalized ``unread_count`` (Doc 03 §9.1); the frozen schema has no last-read
marker. Idempotent and unaudited — see :meth:`InboxService.mark_read`.

Attach existing org tags to a thread (Doc 04 §18.1 v1.3).

Idempotent — a tag already present is a no-op; returns the thread's full tag set. Unknown/foreign
tag → 422; unknown conversation → 404.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a conversation
delete.description: Detach a tag from a thread (Doc 04 §18.1 v1.3). 404 if the conversation or association is absent.

get.description: The caller's personal replies plus all shared ones (Doc 04 §18.2).

post.description: Create a personal (default) or shared canned reply; duplicate shortcut in-scope → 409.

patch.description: Edit shortcut/title/body (partial). Unknown/foreign uuid → 404; shortcut clash → 409.

ApiKeyCreateResponse.title: ApiKeyCreateResponse
ApiKeyCreateResponse.description: Returned once on creation — includes the plaintext secret (never shown again).

BulkDeleteRequest.title: BulkDeleteRequest
BulkDeleteRequest.description: ``POST /contacts/bulk-delete`` — soft-delete over a selection or filter (FR-CON-08).

BulkFilter.title: BulkFilter
BulkFilter.description: A filter that resolves to an audience (Doc 04 §30 addressing mode (b)).

BulkSummary.title: BulkSummary
BulkSummary.description: The §29 summary block; ``processed`` drives the live progress bar (§30).

CampaignEstimateResponse.title: CampaignEstimateResponse
CampaignEstimateResponse.description:
Pre-send cost estimate (FR-CAM-11; Doc 04 §17).

Invariant: ``recipients == sum(b.count for b in breakdown) + unresolved.count``.

CampaignProgressResponse.title: CampaignProgressResponse
CampaignProgressResponse.description:
Live campaign state (FR-CAM-10).

Derived from the roster, which is the authority; the campaign's counters mirror it.

CampaignScheduleRequest.title: CampaignScheduleRequest
CampaignScheduleRequest.description:
When a campaign should fire (Doc 04 §17; FR-CAM-03/04).

One model over three shapes, because they are one decision — "when" — and the fields that do
not apply are simply absent. The service rejects a shape missing what it needs (422).

CampaignScheduleResponse.title: CampaignScheduleResponse
CampaignScheduleResponse.description:
The campaign and the schedule(s) now attached to it (FR-CAM-03/04).

A list, not a single row: a drip request produces one row per step, and returning all of them
is what lets the caller see the sequence it actually created.

CampaignStateResponse.title: CampaignStateResponse
CampaignStateResponse.description: The campaign after a lifecycle transition (Doc 04 §17).

ContactAttributesRequest.title: ContactAttributesRequest
ContactAttributesRequest.description: Set custom attribute values on a contact; ``null`` clears a value (Doc 04 §14.1).

ContactRef.title: ContactRef
ContactRef.description: Who the conversation is with — enough to render an inbox row (Doc 05 B7 pane 2).

ContactTagsRequest.title: ContactTagsRequest
ContactTagsRequest.description: Attach one or more existing tags to a contact (Doc 04 §14.1).

ConversationAssignRequest.title: ConversationAssignRequest
ConversationAssignRequest.description: Assign or reassign a conversation to a user (Doc 04 §18.1).

ConversationMessagesPage.title: ConversationMessagesPage
ConversationMessagesPage.description: A page of a thread's message history (Doc 04 §18.1), newest first.

ConversationReadResponse.title: ConversationReadResponse
ConversationReadResponse.description:
A conversation after its unread counter is reset (Doc 04 §18.1).

Read state in the frozen schema is exactly the denormalized ``unread_count`` (Doc 03 §9.1) —
there is no last-read marker — so this echoes the counter (now ``0``) and the version it settled
at, mirroring the state the sibling write actions return.

ConversationResponse.title: ConversationResponse
ConversationResponse.description: A conversation as the inbox list and detail render it (Doc 04 §18.1).

ConversationStateResponse.title: ConversationStateResponse
ConversationStateResponse.description: A conversation after an assignment or status transition (Doc 04 §18.1).

ConversationTagsRequest.title: ConversationTagsRequest
ConversationTagsRequest.description: Add existing tag(s) to a conversation (Doc 04 §18.1 v1.3).

ConversationTagsResponse.title: ConversationTagsResponse
ConversationTagsResponse.description: A conversation's full tag set after an add (Doc 04 §18.1 v1.3).

ConversationsPage.title: ConversationsPage
ConversationsPage.description: A page of the inbox list (Doc 04 §3 envelope).

EstimateBreakdownEntry.title: EstimateBreakdownEntry
EstimateBreakdownEntry.description:
One priced ``(country, category)`` group (Doc 04 §17).

``unit`` and ``subtotal`` are decimals serialized as fixed-scale strings — a JSON number cannot
carry scale and lands in a binary float, which is what money must never touch.

EstimateUnresolved.title: EstimateUnresolved
EstimateUnresolved.description:
Recipients that could not be priced (Doc 03 §8.5.4).

Reported rather than dropped: excluding them from the total while hiding the count would
understate the number FR-CAM-11 calls exact.

ExportCreateRequest.title: ExportCreateRequest
ExportCreateRequest.description: ``POST /contacts/export`` — filters reuse the segment/search rule shape.

JobAcceptedResponse.title: JobAcceptedResponse
JobAcceptedResponse.description: ``202 Accepted`` — the only response a long-running operation returns (Doc 04 §3).

MediaContentResponse.title: MediaContentResponse
MediaContentResponse.description: A signed, expiring URL for the asset (Doc 04 §16, FR-MED-09).

MediaPayload.title: MediaPayload
MediaPayload.description:
Media to send. Exactly one source — the adapter can only attach one thing.

``media_asset_id`` is the platform's own stored asset (Doc 07 §17.3): it is uploaded to the
channel on the send lane and the resulting id is cached, so the same file sent a hundred times
is uploaded once. ``link``/``media_id`` hand a channel-side reference straight through.

MessageReactionRequest.title: MessageReactionRequest
MessageReactionRequest.description:
React to a message (Doc 04 §18.2 v1.4).

``emoji`` is a **single emoji**; the **empty string** removes a prior reaction. The single-emoji
rule (reject multiple emoji / non-emoji text → ``invalid_emoji``) is enforced in the send service,
which owns the ``422`` code; the length bound here only caps the payload.

MessageSendRequest.title: MessageSendRequest
MessageSendRequest.description:
A send (Doc 04 §18.2).

``type`` selects which payload is read; the others must be absent. Sending is deliberately not
a discriminated union of free-form JSON: the ledger stores canonical content, so what a client
may say is the same shape the adapter is handed.

Page.title: Page
Page.description: The ``page`` object of a collection envelope (Doc 04 §3).

PhoneNumberUpdateRequest.title: PhoneNumberUpdateRequest
PhoneNumberUpdateRequest.description:
``PATCH /phone-numbers/{uuid}`` — operator-owned fields only (Doc 04 §13.3).

Meta-owned facts (quality rating, tier, verified name) are not settable here: they arrive via
sync/refresh, so letting an operator type them would create a lie the next sync silently undoes.

QueuesResponse.title: QueuesResponse
QueuesResponse.description: ``GET /queues`` — depth/throughput per queue plus fleet health (Doc 06 §13.2).

QuickRepliesListResponse.title: QuickRepliesListResponse
QuickRepliesListResponse.description: The visible quick replies (Doc 04 §3 envelope). Bounded per org — not paginated.

QuickReplyCreateRequest.title: QuickReplyCreateRequest
QuickReplyCreateRequest.description: Create a personal or shared quick reply (Doc 04 §18.2).

QuickReplyResponse.title: QuickReplyResponse
QuickReplyResponse.description: A quick reply as returned by the CRUD endpoints (Doc 04 §18.2).

QuickReplyUpdateRequest.title: QuickReplyUpdateRequest
QuickReplyUpdateRequest.description: Edit a quick reply (Doc 04 §18.2). Every field optional — only those present change.

TagSummary.title: TagSummary
TagSummary.description: Compact tag shape embedded in a contact (Doc 04 §14 contact schema).

TemplateButtonPayload.title: TemplateButtonPayload
TemplateButtonPayload.description: A value bound to one of the template's buttons (Doc 04 §18.2 `buttons[]`).

TemplateCreateRequest.title: TemplateCreateRequest
TemplateCreateRequest.description:
A template definition (Doc 04 §15).

``components`` is the platform's own structure — header/body/footer/buttons — validated before
Meta ever sees it. ``submit`` is what separates "save a draft" from "ask Meta"; the default is
to submit, because a template nobody submits can never be sent.

TemplateHeaderMedia.title: TemplateHeaderMedia
TemplateHeaderMedia.description: The file filling a template's media header. Exactly one source, as for a media send.

TemplatePayload.title: TemplatePayload
TemplatePayload.description:
A template send (Doc 04 §18.2).

Values, not components: the caller names the template and supplies the positional variables it
declares. Whether those are approved and correctly counted is the server's business, and what
Graph wants them to look like is the adapter's.

VariableMap.title: VariableMap
VariableMap.description: Mappings positioned to the template's ``{{1}}, {{2}} …``, per component.

VariableMapping.title: VariableMapping
VariableMapping.description:
Where one template variable's value comes from (FR-CAM-01).

``fallback`` matters more than it looks: Meta rejects an empty parameter, so a contact missing
the mapped value would fail the send unless something fills the gap.

WabaCreateRequest.title: WabaCreateRequest
WabaCreateRequest.description: ``POST /waba`` — connect a WABA with its system-user token.

WabaUpdateRequest.title: WabaUpdateRequest
WabaUpdateRequest.description: ``PATCH /waba/{uuid}`` — rotate the token or amend metadata.

WebhookAckResponse.title: WebhookAckResponse
WebhookAckResponse.description:
The body behind a fast ``200``.

Meta only reads the status code, so this exists for operators and tests: it states how many
events the delivery was durably split into (Doc 06 §11.2).

WindowState.title: WindowState
WindowState.description:
The 24-hour customer-service window (Doc 03 §9.1; FR-WA-12).

``is_open`` is computed at read time, not read from the denormalized flag: a window closes by
time passing, not by anything writing a row (Doc 03 §9.1).
